recommendedTextbook.title: Essential Financial Accounting for Senior Secondary Schools
recommendedTextbook.author: R. A. I. Kazeem
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Introduction to Financial Accounting and Ethical Principles
subtopics: History of bookkeeping and double-entry origins (Luca Pacioli, 1494)
Internal and external users of accounting statements (investors, creditors, tax authorities, banks)
Fundamental accounting concepts and conventions (Going concern, accruals, consistency, prudence)
objectives: Define financial accounting and state its primary objectives
Identify 6 users of accounting records and their information requirements
Apply the prudence and consistency concepts to real financial valuation problems

topics.topic: The Accounting Equation and Balance Sheet Mechanics
subtopics: The fundamental equation: ASSETS = CAPITAL + LIABILITIES
Classification of assets (Non-current assets vs current assets) and liabilities (Current vs non-current)
Transaction effects on the accounting equation
objectives: State the accounting equation in its various algebraic forms
Classify 12 commercial balances into assets, capital, and liabilities
Compute changes in owner's equity resulting from revenue earnings and drawings in Naira

topics.topic: Principles of Double Entry and the General Ledger
subtopics: Golden Rules of Debit and Credit for assets, liabilities, income, and expenses
Subdivisions of the Ledger: Sales ledger, purchases ledger, general ledger
Posting commercial transactions and balancing ledger accounts (Balance c/d and b/d)
objectives: Apply debit and credit rules to 15 diverse business transactions
Post journalized entries into personal, real, and nominal ledger accounts
Balance individual ledger accounts at the end of an accounting period

topics.topic: Books of Original Entry and Subsidiary Day Books
subtopics: Subsidiary books: Sales day book, purchases day book, returns inwards/outwards books
The General Journal (Journal Proper): Uses, opening entries, purchase/sale of non-current assets
Format and narrative writing in journal entries
objectives: Record credit transactions in the appropriate subsidiary day books
Draft opening entries in the General Journal with standard narrations
Post subsidiary book totals to the General Ledger control accounts
